Battle of the Centuries (BSD)
description: Do you like fashion? Do you like art? Have you ever wanted to be a model? Have you ever wondered what 9th century royalty wore? Or what was in a roman legionnaires pack? Or any number of profession’s tools of their trade? Or perhaps...you might lean more towards say...the 14th century? The Barony of Sundragon Presents "Battle of the Centuries,” an Arts & Sciences group competition where you can see all those things and more! Work together to present a completed pre 17th century kit while witnessing our talented populace as they showcase their arts on the catwalk. Showing the fashions and professions of centuries long passed. Q&A ~ Competition entries from any pre 17th century era are acceptable. As well as any and all arts & sciences pertaining to your entry. Pre-prepared food is allowed as part of your entry. ~ Groups may consist of one or more people. ~ All entries must have a model or equivalent, yes mannequins are permitted. ~ Entries for the competition must provide basic documentation. ~ A fashion show with a vocal presentation will take place. ~ A photo op area will be available. ~ THE SITE IS DRY ~ Tables for displays will be available for those that do not wish to compete. ~ There will be an overall winner, a populace choice, best dressed, and best in category. We want to see the stitches, we want to see the tools, the accoutrements of the ages! We want to see the arts that you love. So come and compete at Sundragons BATTLE OF THE CENTURIES!

title: Calafia Anniversary
location: El Monte Park, 15805 El Monte Rd, Lakeside, CA 92040
description: Come join the Barony of Calafia at our “New Year’s Harvest” Anniversary event. Our theme this year is inspired by the Navajo season of Gháájí' , which translates to “half” and describes the separation of seasons between Summer and Winter. This is not only our New Year with the rise of the first new moon , but also the end of the harvest season. We invite the populace to show off your harvest best and celebrate the beginning of Calafia’s new year with us! SCHEDULE : 7:30am - Site opens for set up 8am - Gate opens 8:30am - Lysts opens 9am - Opening court (at Their Excellencies leisure) 3:30pm - Closing court (at Their Excellencies leisure) 5pm - Site closes (must be off site) EVENT REGISTRATION : Adult Event Registration, $25. Adult Member Discount Event Registration, $15. Youth under 18 are guests of the Barony. Cash and checks accepted at gate. Make checks payable to “SCA Inc./Barony of Calafia”. The county charges a $3 fee per car at the park entrance, cash only. COMBAT SCENARIOS : There will be competitions for Armored, Rapier, Cut & Thrust, and Youth combat, to select the Baronial Champions for the upcoming year. We will not have Archery or Thrown Weapons at Anniversary this year - both of those competitions will instead be held during the Calafia Equestrian Championship event in December. ACTIVITIES : Activities will include a Dirty Dozen competition, the ever-popular “Taste of Calafia” brewers competition, a mini-Archery range, and more! Details will be announced on the FB event page when available. DIRTY DOZEN LARGESSE COMPETITION : There will be a Dirty Dozen Largesse Competition this year. The winner will be announced at closing court and prizes to be disseminated afterward. Each participant will be able to pick a prize in the order of their ranking. Entrants are advised to create 12 items based on a theme that is suitable for largesse. For example: 12 needle books, 12 hats from different (or the same) period(s), 12 items suitable for a specific time period, 12 children’s toys, etc. Note: items that traditionally are used in pairs should include twelve pairs, so 12 socks are not suitable as it is only 6 pairs. All entries should be tagged with the item type, artisan’s name and province, and be ready to be given the day of the competition. Items do not need to be documented as this is not an Arts and Sciences competition. Items should not have heraldry on them as they are meant to be presented in other areas. Judging will be done by the populace in the following manner: Each entrant display will have a cup placed next to it. During the event, anyone may put a provided token into the cup accompanying their choice. Once voting closes, and all votes have been tallied, the entrant with the most tokens in their cup gets the first choice of 3 items from any of the entries as a prize. Each subsequent entrant then chooses from the remaining entries in order, according to the popular vote. Each entry may only be chosen once as a prize. The remaining 11 items from each entry will be given to Their Excellencies for use as largesse. TASTE OF CALAFIA: Calafia's Anniversary is Saturday, October 10 and The Calafian Brewers Guild will be holding a "Taste of Calafia" in the same manner as was done at Potrero. All submissions need to be a fermented (Ales, Meads, Ciders, Etc.) or non-alcoholic drink, as this will ensure we meet the rules of the site. (No Cordials or mixed drinks). Minimum size should be at least 22oz or bigger. If you would like to submit a drink for the event please let me or Triona know so we can get an idea of the numbers and styles that will be offered. Please reach out with any questions. CALAFIA ARCHERY: Calafia Archery is excited to welcome Order of the Mark Vigilant, Ronan de Bhal, as he hosts a special mini‑archery range booth as part of his wandering vigil. All ages are welcome to stop by and take a few shots on the mini range — no experience needed, just a smile and a willingness to have a bit of fun with our suction‑cup arrows and rubber‑band bows. It’s a perfect chance to share in the joy of archery and celebrate this wonderful moment with Vigilant Ronan. LUNCH : Food will be prepared and provided by the Willie family clan and its matriarch. Lunch will feature a modern take on traditional homestyle foods eaten at this seasonal change. Vegetarian options will be offered, water will be available. Please bring your feast gear. $10 suggested donation. SITE INFORMATION/RESTRICTIONS : This is a damp site. Smoking, including vapes, is prohibited on park grounds. Pets are welcome but must be leashed at all times. If you are a visiting barony or if your group is planning on bringing a pavilion, please email the event stewards no later than September 27th, so we can make sure you have enough space. MERCHANTS : Merchants are welcome but must have a CA seller’s permit. Contact the event stewards for information. EVENT STEWARDS : Noble Ádeezbáá, dxʷdəwʔabš nishłį́ Tł’ízídaalchí’í bashishchiin & THLady Adella Silberfpeil EVENT EMAIL : - caid.org DIRECTIONS : From the north, west, and south. Take I-8 East to exit 17B onto CA-67 North. Go for 5.8 miles then keep right onto Mapleview St. Continue on Mapleview St/Lake Jennings Park Rd for 0.6 miles then make a sharp left onto El Monte Rd (by the 7/11). The park is 4 miles down on the right

description: Hearken, fair Atlantia, and let great rejoicing fill the land! As autumn's golden mantle settles upon the realm and the harvest season draws to its close, the Barony of Dun Carraig bids all nobles, gentles, artisans, warriors, and wanderers welcome to a weekend of celebration, fellowship, and pageantry. Join us October 30 – November 1, 2026, as we witness the Investiture of our new Baronage and mark the beginning of a new chapter in the history of our beloved Barony. Come gather beneath banners flying proudly in the crisp autumn air as Their Excellencies take up the mantle of leadership. Let voices be raised in acclamation, cups lifted in good cheer, and friendships renewed around hearth and table. The lists shall come alive with displays of valor as armored combatants contest for honor and glory, while rapier fighters test their skill and courtesy upon the field. Archers and throwers alike are invited to demonstrate their precision and prowess upon the ranges, proving that steady hands and keen eyes are as worthy as strength of arm. Those with a love of the arts and sciences are encouraged to attend in their finest attire. Let the fields and halls be adorned with elegant cotehardies, splendid kirtles, graceful hoods, and all manner of medieval finery befitting the season. Whether clad in humble wool or noble silk, all are welcome to share in the beauty and inspiration of our Society. As evening falls, gather for a sumptuous feast where good company, laughter, and excellent fare shall abound. Tales will be told, songs will be sung, and memories made to last through many winters to come. In keeping with the festive spirit of the season, all are invited to participate in our Pet Costume Contest! Bring forth your most noble hounds or any beloved (toy) companion bedecked in medieval splendor, heraldic glory, or harvest merriment. Prizes and admiration await those creatures most charmingly attired. Whether you come seeking martial renown, artistic inspiration, delicious fare, or simply the joy of gathering among friends, there shall be a place for you at our celebration. So don your finest garb , prepare your banners, and make haste to Dun Carraig. Together let us honor the past, celebrate the present, and welcome our new Baronage with all the pomp, ceremony, and merriment that such an occasion deserves. By our hands and hearts, we invite you to join us for this grand and joyous Investiture Weekend. October 30 – November 1, 2026 Vivat Atlantia! Vivat Dun Carraig! Vivat Their Excellencies!

title: Dance Practice
location: Holy Trinity Armenian Church, 145 Brattle St, Cambridge, MA 02138, USA
description: Come join us at Carolingian Dance Practice! The Autumn 2026 practices will be on Tuesdays (a bit scattered due to site and teacher availability): Sept 15th, Oct 27th, Nov 17th, and Dec 15th. This is a fun social occasion for all: an evening where we all get together to learn Renaissance Dances and socialize with the members of the Barony. It is specifically newcomer-friendly: all dances are taught, you don’t need to come with a partner (we encourage folks to switch partners from dance to dance), and folks generally come in street clothes. Just wear something comfortable that you can move in (especially comfortable shoes). We meet from 7:30 – 9:30pm at the Holy Trinity Armenian Church, at 145 Brattle Street in Cambridge. There’s a parking lot for those who need to drive, bus routes nearby, and it’s less than a 20 minute walk from the Harvard Square MBTA station. The parking lot is off of Sparks Street, on the far side of the Church away from Brattle Street. (If using a GPS, 62 Sparks Street is roughly across the street from the parking lot.) The hall where we will be dancing is next to the parking lot, so if you are walking up Brattle Street, turn onto Sparks Street to get to the hall. If the front door on Sparks Street is locked, come around to the parking lot side and use the door there. Dances are taught and called using the gender-free “Larks and Robins” style, popular with many of the local dance communities. We have a lot of space (easily twice what we need for dancing), so folks are welcome to come bring other SCA activities for the sidelines, or even to just come hang out! The site costs $100 per session; donations are optional, but welcome to help defray the cost of renting the hall. So come join us! It’s very much “the more, the merrier”, and you’re very welcome to join in!

description: We hope you can join us for Falling Leaves and our Baronial Archery and Thrown Weapons Championships! Come hang out with friends, tackle some targets, and check out some of the activities the SCA has to offer. In addition to the Baronial Champs competitions there will be Equestrian, Rattan and Rapier Tourneys, Music & Dancing, Merchants, and Youth Activities. (More details to come). **UPDATE: Due to age and injury (of horses, not people) we will be unable to have a joust this year. We hope to return next year with the next generation of EK Jousting steeds!** • THIS IS A DRY SITE, NO ALCOHOL IS TO BE CONSUMED ON THE SITE GROUNDS • There will NOT BE a dayboard available at this event, but there will be a snack table! Please bring whatever kind of picnic lunch you would like! All activities will be paused around mid-day so that we may all enjoy some food! •Site is pet friendly, but please consider keeping pets away from the Equestrian rings since horses can be spooked easily. •If you wish to bring your horse(s) to this event, please contact the Equestrian Marshal-in-Charge, Cathain Reiter (209013@members.eastkingdom.org) PRIOR to the event. Per the site, current negative Coggins and inter-state health certificate are required. Currently the site is asking these to be made available 2 weeks prior to the event. These should be submitted to the Equestrian Marshal-in-Charge in advance via email. •Any merchants wishing to attend please contact the event steward & merchant coordinator (Contact info listed at bottom of this post) directly for space allocation. TOURNAMENT DETAILS: RAPIER: • 3 v 3 Melee Tournament • Round & Round Robin Tournament • Live Steel A&S Experiment Rapier fighters will have the opportunity to participate in both a melee and singles tournament, with a bonus live steel stabbing experiment (of ballistic gel. Not humans.) ARMORED: For Armored Combat activities, our schedule includes a morning tournament, followed by an afternoon of 3v3 Melee, Tavern Brawling, and The Wheel Of Pain, should our fighters still be ready and in high enough number. Tournament Format: The morning tournament shall consist of 3 rounds. Round 1: The assembled combatants will line up by Order of Precedence. The method of pairing for this round will be by the issuance of Challenge: The combatant of the lowest award level shall be given the first opportunity to issue a challenge to any other combatant in the tournament, regardless of award level. This is followed by the next lowest award level combatant issuing a challenge, and so on, until all fighters have issued a challenge or have been challenged. (In the event of an uneven number, the unchallenged fighter will receive a ‘bye’ for that set of challenges). Upon acceptance of a challenge, the two combatants will report to the marshall within an available list to conduct their bout. Each bout this round is single pass, with any double kills refought until a victor is determined. The defeated combatant will have a loss recorded. After completing their fight, combatants are to return to form a line by Order of Precedence. Once every combatant has fought their first bout, challenges again shall be issued in a similar manner. Once a combatant accrues 3 losses, they are eliminated from the tournament. Challenges will be issued until we have a final four combatants remaining. Round 2: Fighters are again lined up by Order of Precedence. The right of first challenge goes to the combatant of the lowest award level. Each fight will be best 2 of 3 passes. All double kills to be refought until a victor is determined. The weapons forms will be matched, and the choice of forms is determined by combatants who are NOT fighting that bout. The winners of these fights advance to the finals. Final Round: The Finals shall be determined in a best three of five passes, with all double kills being refought. The weapons forms shall be matched, and the form will be chosen by those watching, with no form chosen twice. (Note: A choice of 'Fighter's Best' is an acceptable reason to return to a form again.) To this end, the Marshal In Charge will select from the assembled someone to choose the form for each pass. The winner of this round will be declared the overall winner of the tournament. ARCHERY CHAMPIONSHIPS: The competition shooting is open to ALL archers who are already familiar with range safety and have some SCA archery experience; others are encouraged to attend the Archery Newcomers Hour. Finalists will be the top scorers who agree to the Carolingian Champions Agreement. Archers may shoot the parts of the competition at any time before 2pm. Archers can do each shoot as often as their energy and time permit, and submit their best score on each. **SCHEDULE** 9:00am: Site officially OPENS 9:00am - 2:00pm: Archery Championship Qualifiers 9:30am: Heavy MOL and Inspections opens 10:00am: Equestrian Auths and WarmUps begin 10:00am: Thrown Weapons Championship Qualifiers begin 10:00am - 2:00pm: Stab a Dummy! title: Fellowship of the Argent Angel Anniversary Event (Windy Meads)

description: On a quiet Sunday afternoon in September 1995, nine friends solemnly pledged themselves to each other, agreeing to participate in an exploration of the concept of Chivalry by striving to do our best, while never sacrificing honor for base gain or the sake of vanity. Those nine – Obadiah, Gareth, Alden, Wiglaf, Thorfinn, Kolbyr, Helgi, Kayla, and Stephen – proclaimed themselves The Fellowship of the Argent Angel, taking for device an Angel armed as for war, Argent, and for motto “Quisque Custodiat Quemque.” Thirty summers have passed since that fateful day, and still our Fellowship aspires to ideals beyond our reach. We have lost two beloved brothers: Mathias and Obadiah, and happily welcomed eighteen more. It is now our desire to stand the field in celebration of our decades of commitment to each other and the glorious ideal of Chivalry. Do not mistake us! We do not stand with Prideful presumption that we have achieved the ideals to which we strive, only that we acknowledge the joy of the quest and would welcome other like-minded gentles to join us in celebration of our collective aspirations. Therefore shall we stand the field and present to our noble Gallery, with all appropriate pageantry and honor, a passage of armes. The passage shall commence with a helm schau, providing the Gallery the opportunity to offer their favor to our gentle venans. Then, words of welcome will be spoken, introductions made, and first passes commenced. Thereafter, the Gallery will choose the manner and making of each challenge, regaling all with inspiration from the era that inspires us. Provision will be provided to assist with such challenges, as desired. Challenges shall be made and met throughout the afternoon, interrupted occasionally with melee contests of all participants. The passage shall be deemed complete after a rigorous contest at the barrier and appropriate closing words. The remainder of the day and evening shall be spent sharing memories of joyful days, past and present. Additional Comments: Entry into the Tournament upon $25 donation to The Cartmel Priory Trust per combatant. Gate fee includes admittance and access to the gallery and dayboard. Reservations may be forwarded with advance gate fee to Event Steward. Reservations will be held only with advance payment. Event space is limited to the first 125 people confirming their reservations. Tournament is limited to the first 30 entrants.

description: Both Armored Combat and Rapier fighter practice are held Saturdays, 8am-10am, near Ramada #11 (SE side) of Caballero Park in Yuma, AZ. For notices of cancellation please check our calendar and our Facebook group! If you are interested in combat sports and martial arts, come give it a try! We have loaner gear available, just let us know you are interested by emailing our marshal at .org or posting to our Facebook group! Note you will want to bring your own hard-shelled sports cup (groin protection namely for males) and maybe wear long sleeved clothing. Otherwise, we have everything else you need, you just have to show up! You must be 16 and older to participate and must sign a waiver for liability purposes at every practice unless you are a paid member and authorized to fight in the SCA. Participants under 18 years old must have a parent or legal guardian present to sign a waiver and consent form. What to expect your first time at a fighter practice: We will go over all safety requirements and procedures before having you (or your parent/legal guardian) sign a waiver. Then we will help you get armored up from our loaners appropriate for armored combat or rapier, depending on your expressed interest. We then will do an armor inspection to make sure your armor meets minimum requirements and is safe. Next, we will help calibrate, which involves delivering a blow to your person to help you understand the varying degrees of force used, i.e. what is considered light, good, and excessive. We will go over some basic rules including what striking areas are legal or not. Next, we will go over and practice some basic stances and techniques to make sure you can safely deliver a blow and defend yourself. Finally, we let you have a go at it and see what you can do! Many first timers struggle with having an idea in there head of what is going to happen and executing that idea the way they pictured it. More often than not it almost never works out the way you imagined it, and that is okay! That shouldn’t discourage you from trying something that sounds cool in your head, sometimes it works out and can surprise even the most seasoned of fighters! We are all students and teachers here, even you, and we learn the most when we humble ourselves to those facts. For more information on safety and rules, please refer to the SCA Armored Combat (Rattan) Marshals Handbook and/or Atenveldt Rapier Handbook found in the Kingdom Document Library [RECURRING — also on: 5 Sep 2026, 12 Sep 2026, 19 Sep 2026, 26 Sep 2026, 3 Oct 2026, 10 Oct 2026, 17 Oct 2026, 24 Oct 2026]

description: Once a year the veil between worlds grows thin, and ancient roads, long lost to time emerge in the misty foothills of Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains. From the hidden places of history—where mysticism, superstition, and the macabre ruled the Middle Ages—an autumn market faire took root at the crossroads of forgotten paths between our world and long forgotten realms. Here at the confluence of time stands a place where treasures are exchanged, memories are honored, and history comes alive. Over the rolling hills of Virginia's wine country the waxing moon reveals pathways leading to this archaic place. Passing beyond the threshold of time, wanderers and traders from the medieval world converge. Viking storytellers, Celtic mystics, Moorish scholars, and Mongol horsemen arrive to share skills, goods, secrets, and stories. Some bring offerings for the dead, others seek wisdom from spirits who linger beyond the veil. The journey will be dangerous, so disguise yourself in attire to blend in with the medieval denizens of this market. You may find yourself learning arts thought long lost, trading tokens from another realm, unearthing forgotten tales by firelight, or discovering customs of undiscovered lands. Will you walk among the traders of forgotten civilizations? Carry home a relic from another age? Or perhaps even depart to another time, eventually returning to the present changed, haunted by whispers of those who once stood in your place? Harvest Market is a hybrid public/private event held in partnership with Mountain Run Winery in Culpeper, VA. From 12:00-5:00 pm SCA members and vendors will conduct a demonstration and market open to the public free of charge. The public can take classes and view demonstrations/displays that include archery, thrown weapons, youth combat, arts, sciences, and games. There will be a Halloween-themed costume contest. Food trucks will be on site. At 5:00 the site will be closed to the public for a private SCA event. SCA members, vendors, and non-members who pay the site fee are welcome to stay for a night of revelry. A court and medievel-themed costume contest will begin the evening accompanied by music by DragonSong in the Greenlee Tavern. From 7:00-9:00 roasted meats, stew, bread, and potatoes will be available for those who pay the feast fee. Welcome all who dare to travel forgotten paths before they fade back in to the autumn mists of the Virginia foothills.

description: The Cook Inlet is in need of a Pirate Lord! The Barony of Selviergard will be hosting their Warlord Tournaments to find the Baronial Warlord and Baronial Defender and the event will have games and competitions to determine which Buccaneer Captain or Sea Dog will serve as the Baronesses of Selviergard’s Corsair Commodore of the Cook Inlet! The goal of the Commodore of the Cook Inlet will be to acquire the most treasure through games of chance and tournament. The competitions will include Armored Combat Tournament, Rapier Tournament, a Thrown Weapons Tournament and Pirate themed games of chance. The most profitable pirate from the Games and Tournaments will be named Dread Pirate Lord of Selviergard and Commodore of the Corsairs of the Cook Inlet! The site tokens will be a small bag of coins with which to engage in gaining your wealth. Victories in the combat styles win coins from your opponents and the gaming tables will be set up under Pavilion B for those who wish to earn their gold through chance. The fighting for Hard Suit and Rapier will be aboard ship in a Bear Pit Style with wounds carrying over. Each time a fighter enters the ship to fight, they pay one coin to board, the winner of the pass at arms keeping the coins. The victorious fighter stays aboard and pays another coin to fight the next opponent, retaining any wounds suffered. Falling overboard is fatal, and if both fighters do so, their coins remain on the ship for the next pair to fight over. The Populace will be able to intervene on behalf of the fighters by paying for the ship’s surgeon to heal severed limbs and injured body parts. The Ship’s Surgeon being interested in being paid the most for such services will auction off the healing to the highest bidder. If the fighter they paid to heal wins the next pass at arms, the populace member who paid for the healing doubles the cost of the medical aid, if that fighter loses the cost is lost. Fighters are not allowed to pay for their own healing, but may pay for another fighter’s healing. A Saving the Crew from the Terrifying Sea Monster with Thrown Weapons Tournament will be held. Harpoons will be purchased to cast at the Monster and successfully slaying it doubles your money; however, if you injure one of the crew you must pay double! A Pirate themed Arts and Sciences Challenges will also be part of the fun. The Arts and Sciences will be Pirate Flags! One contest will be crafting the best Pirate Flag from materials provided on site the other will be for best prepared flag brought from home. Additionally you may bring any Pirate themed artistic project you wish to display at a Populace Choice competition, completed or in progress. There will be contests for the most impressive pirate costume with a gangplank walk during the feast. The Feast will be a potluck Competition Feast with the Populace bringing their best Chili or Stew to share and the dishes judged by Populace Choice for best overall, the winning Chef winning a prize and bragging rights for the entire winter! The site is dry. No camping allowed. We may raise tents for the day for shade and activities. The site is close to the privies but not right next to them. We will not have any fires. We are asking the Populace to bring propane stoves for heating up your chili and stews. Lake Lucille Park is an active bear area, so plan to be Bear Aware!

title: Samhain (Selviergard)

description: Good travelers, check your baggage, light your lanterns, and prepare to cross the threshold. This year, we gather at the beautiful, historic Palmer Train Depot, transformed for the evening into a bustling medieval waystation at the edge of the known world. title: The Silver Wyvern Challenge II and Smoking Rocks 50th Birthday
location: Camp Haiastan 722 Summer Street Franklin, MA 02038 US
description: The Star of the Northern Army has made shields tremble and swords waver for nearly 30 years. Before that star, there was another banner that inspired equal awe upon the field… that of The Silver Wyvern, Master Feral Von Halstern. Though he now keeps court in Valhalla, his legacy remains woven into the fabric of the East and lives on in all who pursue the call of honor and glory. Now, as we honor both his memory and the enduring legacy of those who follow in his footsteps, the Barony of Smoking Rocks once again call the populace to gather. Join us as we celebrate the return of a challenge worthy of The Silver Wyvern and mark a milestone in the history of the Barony itself. We invite all to the return of The Silver Wyvern Challenge and celebrate the 50th Birthday of the Barony. We welcome you to our vision of Dorstad Village. Participate in contests of skill, displays of artistry, wander the market for merchants' wares, feast till your bellies are full, and enjoy the abundance of fellowship as we welcome the return of The Silver Wyvern Challenge and celebrate the past 50 years. Their Excellencies are pleased to announce that they are seeking new Arts & Sciences and Fencing Champions at this event. Fencing format will be announced soon. The A&S competition has been defined by the Barony’s current Champion, Layden Octavia Verita. She has specified that entries must have started within the 18 months preceding the event and documentation is not required. Please note that alcoholic beverages may not be served, sampled, or distributed as an entry for the A&S competition. Dorstad Marketplace: Come and set up your wares in the central pavilion of the village to create our own marketplace, there is not a fee to merchant, but we ask that you preregister for the event and to secure your space using this form https://forms.gle/5w3sZd3yZjAvpR4p9 ! Please reach out to Kadlin with any questions or comments at 302240@members.eastkingdom.org Dorstad Village is located at the beautiful Camp Haiastan, in Franklin MA. The site offers buildings that include cabins, feast hall, activity locations, and bathrooms with showers (On demand hot water!) It is also as ADA compliant as a wilderness camp can be with roads, ramps, and paths, to all locations. The site is easily accessible by highway and is within a 15-minute drive from Hotels, Banks, Restaurants, Grocery and Liquor stores! Yes, the site is discreetly damp. Please keep beverages to period drinkware and do not leave cans, bottles, or other trash around site. No yelling, “Who wants Whiskey!?!” and remember to drink responsibly or you will be asked to leave site. Cabins are furnished with bunk beds and can sleep up to four, eight, or twelve people depending on the cabin. They do have power outlets, but camp has set the expectation that only cell phones and medical devices are to be plugged in. The camp does not allow heaters, coffee makers, or other electronics that draw power outside of medically needed devices in the cabins. Food and smoking/vapes of any kind are not allowed in the cabins as well. Cabin rentals will be reservation only and non-refundable but may be transferred to another preregistered guest. There is also limited tent space with preregistration required, there is no extra charge for tent camping. Site Opens: October 23 at 5pm Site Closes: October 25 at 12pm

description: For Twelfth Night 2027, the populace is invited to celebrate a season of transition, where old traditions and joyful excess meet at the turning of the year. The theme draws inspiration from late medieval southern Germany and Switzerland, where winter observances blended seamlessly with lively seasonal celebrations marking the close of one cycle and the promise of the next. By the fifteenth century, these celebrations had fused into a distinctive blend of formality and fun. Daytime brought courtly pomp, displays of skill, and structured ceremony, while nightfall ushered in feasting, dancing, and masked revelry. This balance of order and exuberance provides the perfect setting for Atlantia’s Twelfth Night, offering a full day of pageantry and arts followed by an evening devoted to celebration, community, and unapologetic joy. During this time, the days surrounding Twelfth Night marked the end of the winter holiday season and the gradual shift toward spring. Communities gathered for pageantry, symbolic acts of renewal, and public festivities that reflected both reflection and anticipation. These moments were as much about community and tradition as they were about marking time itself. Alongside this came Fasnacht, a vibrant pre Lenten carnival that preserved much older seasonal customs. Masquerades, mummers, and playful processions filled towns with music, laughter, and satire. Masks and costumes allowed for mischief and creativity, and the rules of everyday life were happily bent before the long quiet of late winter.
